name: Classical false-position scalar root solver
definition: Check endpoint zeros first. Given a<b and opposite signs f(a), f(b), compute x=(af(b)−bf(a))/(f(b)−f(a)). If f(x)=0 return x; otherwise replace the endpoint of matching sign with x and repeat. Return a bracket on width tolerance, or a residual-only approximate point explicitly labelled as such.
variables: a,b ordered bracket endpoints; x interpolation trial; f real scalar function
assumptions: Continuous real f, strict sign change after endpoint-zero checks, finite values, representable interior trials and bounded iterations
limitations: A bracket endpoint may remain fixed indefinitely; a small residual alone is not a certified error bound without further assumptions
failure_conditions: Invalid bracket, nonfinite arithmetic, noninterior trial due to rounding, stagnation or iteration budget exceeded
computation: Compute the secant intercept with guarded arithmetic, then update by sign rather than multiplying potentially extreme residuals. Keep the bracket invariant; distinguish a residual stopping rule from width certification.

source.citation: Vladimir Dobrushkin, Brown University, Mathematica tutorial, Part III Bracketing Methods, section II False Position Method. https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/dobrush/am33/python/p3/bracket.html

required_inputs: Continuous scalar function, sign-changing bracket and tolerances.
mechanism_note: Same linear intercept as the existing secant method, but retains the opposite-sign endpoint rather than discarding by age. Bracket preservation is a material control-rule change; counted as a variant, not an independent algorithm.

name: Open inverse quadratic scalar root iteration
definition: For three points x_i with distinct y_i=f(x_i), set x_new=Σ_i x_i Π_(j≠i) (−y_j)/(y_i−y_j); discard the oldest point and repeat unless converged.
variables: Three recent iterates x_i and their function values y_i=f(x_i)
assumptions: Three distinct finite function values; local smoothness and a simple root for useful convergence.
limitations: No bracket guarantee; close function values can produce unstable extrapolation.
failure_conditions: Coincident function values, nonfinite or divergent iterate, or exhausted budget
computation: Provisional inverse Lagrange interpolation at y=0; check standalone novelty against Brent before admission.

source.citation: Driscoll and Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, section 4.4.2 Inverse interpolation. https://fncbook.com/secant/

required_inputs: Scalar function, three initial points, stopping tolerances and iteration budget
incompatible_methods: Assuming an invariant bracket or global convergence
mechanism_note: Standalone open control differs from Brent, but the inverse quadratic interpolation kernel is already included in Brent. Retained in candidate archive, not counted.
